question: Can frozen 500K GPTrans encoder states identify a readout-information bottleneck behind weak scale-transfer gains?

hypothesis.observed_deficiency: Three positive 100K GPTrans mechanisms retain only 1-2 meV of gain against the matched 500K baseline.
alternative_explanations: Baseline catches up with more optimization and data.
The selected heads were optimized jointly with their encoders; a frozen probe may miss an end-to-end interaction.
hypothesis.changed_mechanism: No encoder change; compare frozen-feature residual readouts with and without mean real-atom states.
hypothesis.cheapest_falsifier: First inspect the four aligned retained prediction artifacts and accepted 500K traces without retraining.
hypothesis.decision_changed_if_positive: Prioritize a separately contracted end-to-end readout study over more anti-collapse regularizers.
hypothesis.decision_changed_if_negative: Do not claim a frozen-readout cause; investigate optimization, data-scale and generalization separately.
historical_unknowns: The development role has already been selected on repeatedly.
Local extraction runtime is not yet measured.

next_allowed_actions: No automatic successor; reconcile the separate existing DSAR route before any new readout training.
reopen_conditions: A new, separately frozen 500K causal contract and budget are justified by independent evidence.

comparison_blockers: Post-hoc reuse of a development role already used for selection.
No new end-to-end 500K training or independent seed.
